operation_details.item: The user always stays on free-tier design software and avoids paid collaboration features even on multi-designer client projects.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How is the client project shaping up today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well. I’m refining a visual system with hand-built textures and some cultural references rather than leaning on the usual polished, minimalist look.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That sounds distinctive. Are you working with anyone else on the deliverables?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, there are a few designers contributing. I’m keeping us on the free tier of our design software, though—I avoid paid collaboration features even when a project has multiple designers.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How are you coordinating without the paid tools?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: We exchange exported files, leave notes in a shared document, and do short review calls. It takes a little more organization, but it works for our process.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. Are the client deliverables mostly presentation pieces or production-ready assets?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: A mix of both. I’m making the presentation feel expressive while keeping the final assets practical for the client to use.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For design software subscriptions, I always stay on free tiers and avoid paid collaboration features even on multi-designer client projects.
